- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.4), model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid excessive sell-off bias.
- After a recent price spike, model often overshoots downward in the next 5–10 days; apply a mild upward bias to counteract lagged sell-off momentum.
- If sentiment is positive and price is trending up, model frequently underestimates the continuation; add 1–2% buffer to forecast for momentum carry.
- Mean reversion is overemphasized in model; if recent 10-day average is significantly above or below 30-day average, reduce forecast deviation from that anchor.
- For 30-day horizon, model underpredicts true price in early days (1–7) when sentiment is volatile; increase forecast slightly for first 3–5 days to capture sentiment-driven volatility.
- When sentiment swings sharply (e.g., from +0.3 to -0.5), model fails to adjust quickly; apply a 2–3 day lag correction to align with sentiment shift direction.
